name: iBoxDB
tagline: Embedded transactional table-style document database for Java and .NET, including Android and Unity.
description: iBoxDB is an embedded NoSQL database with separate pure-Java and pure-.NET engines and no native dependencies, so the same data model runs in desktop apps, ASP.NET Core and Blazor servers, Android, Xamarin and Unity games. Data lives in tables that hold documents with dynamic columns, composite keys, and unique or non-unique indexes; each 'box' is an isolated transaction committed explicitly, with snapshot-serializable isolation, and queries use a small SQL-like syntax, key lookups, LINQ on .NET or streams on Java. The developer also builds a full-text search server on it. The .NET package reached 4.1.1 in August 2026. The license terms are not published on the site, so confirm them with the developer before shipping a commercial product.

license.name: Proprietary (free download; license terms not published)

pricing.notes: Freely downloadable from the website, NuGet and GitHub examples; no published price list.

scale.notes: In-process database for a single application; no clustering.

strengths: Pure Java and pure .NET engines with no native dependencies
Runs on Android, Unity, Xamarin and server runtimes from one data model
Snapshot-serializable ACID transactions in an embedded store
Dynamic columns and composite keys in table-style documents
weaknesses: License terms are not clearly published
Small, mostly single-developer ecosystem with sparse English documentation
No replication or server mode for multi-process access
useCases: Local storage for Unity or Godot games
Embedded storage inside Java or .NET services
notIdealFor: Teams that need a clear open-source license
